content:
We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with 3 reactions for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We have guidance: three steps correspond to forward reactions: 1) amide formation (carboxylic acid + amine). 2) Doebner modification (aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated acid). 3) sulfonamide formation (amine + sulfonyl chloride). So retrosynthetic steps: break amide bond to give carboxylic acid and aniline (or amine). Then break the α,β-unsaturated acid to give aldehyde and malonic acid? Actually Doebner modification forward: aromatic aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid (the double bond). So retrosynthesis: the unsaturated acid fragment (C= C C(=O)N...) came from aldehyde + malonic acid. So we need to disconnect the C=C bond and the amide carbonyl? Wait the unsaturated acid is part of the chain: /C=C/C(=O)N... So the α,β-unsaturated acid is the product of Doebner: aromatic aldehyde (maybe p-? ) plus malonic acid gives trans-α,β-unsaturated acid (cinnamic acid derivative). So in our target, the unsaturated acid is attached to aromatic ring (c2ccc(... )cc2). So the fragment is a phenyl ring with a trans-α,β-unsaturated carboxamide attached. So retrosynthesis: break the C=C double bond to give aldehyde (aryl aldehyde) and malonic acid (or its derivative). Then amide formation: the carboxylic acid (from Doebner) reacts with aniline (Nc3ccccc3N) to give amide. Finally sulfonamide formation: the aniline (the first phenyl with methyl) reacts with sulfonyl chloride (SO2Cl) to give sulfonamide linking to the second phenyl.

Thus we need to propose three steps: Step1 (retro) sulfonamide cleavage: target -> sulfonyl chloride (maybe p-toluenesulfonyl chloride?) Actually the sulfonyl group is attached to the first phenyl (with methyl). The sulfonyl group is attached to the nitrogen linking to second phenyl. So we can break N-S bond to give sulfonyl chloride (or sulfonyl acid) and the amine (the first phenyl with NH). So precursor1: p-tolyl amine (4-methyl aniline) (Cc1ccc(N)cc1). Precursor2: sulfonyl chloride attached to second phenyl? Actually the sulfonyl group is attached to the second phenyl ring (c2ccc...). The sulfonyl group is attached to nitrogen which is attached to the second phenyl. So the sulfonyl chloride would be something like ClSO2-Ph-... but the sulfonyl group is attached to the second phenyl ring (the one bearing the unsaturated amide). So the sulfonyl chloride precursor would be something like ClSO2-c2ccc(... )cc2 (i.e., aryl sulfonyl chloride). So step1: target -> 4-methyl aniline + aryl sulfonyl chloride (aryl-SO2Cl). Step2: break amide: the aryl sulfonyl chloride still has the unsaturated amide attached to it? Wait the amide is attached to the unsaturated acid attached to the same phenyl (c2...). So after step1, we have aryl sulfonyl chloride bearing the unsaturated acid? Actually the sulfonyl chloride is attached to the nitrogen which is attached to the unsaturated amide side chain. In the target, the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to the sulfonyl group (SO2) and to the first phenyl (methyl phenyl). The other side of the sulfonyl group is attached to the second phenyl (c2...). So the sulfonyl chloride precursor would be something like ClSO2-c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2 (aryl sulfonyl chloride). So step1: cleavage yields 4-methyl aniline and aryl sulfonyl chloride.

Step2: amide formation retrosynthesis: break amide bond between carbonyl and aniline (Nc3ccccc3N). So we get carboxylic acid (the unsaturated acid) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). So precursor: aryl sulfonyl chloride (from step1) still has the unsaturated acid attached? Actually the unsaturated acid is part of the same molecule as the sulfonyl chloride. So after step2, we have aryl sulfonyl chloride (same) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). Wait the amide is attached to the unsaturated acid which is attached to the aryl sulfonyl chloride. So after breaking amide, we get the unsaturated acid (c2ccc(/C=C/COOH)cc2) attached to sulfonyl group? Actually the sulfonyl group is attached to the nitrogen of the unsaturated acid? No, the sulfonyl group is attached to the nitrogen that is attached to the first phenyl. The unsaturated amide is attached to the second phenyl via the carbonyl nitrogen (N attached to phenyl). So the sulfonyl group is not directly attached to the unsaturated acid; it's attached to the nitrogen linking the two phenyls. So after breaking amide, we get the unsaturated acid attached to the second phenyl (c2ccc(/C=C/COOH)cc2) and the aniline (c3ccccc3N). The sulfonyl group remains attached to the first phenyl? Wait the sulfonyl group is attached to the nitrogen that also attaches to the first phenyl. So after amide cleavage, the sulfonyl group is still attached to the first phenyl? Actually the sulfonyl group is attached to the nitrogen that is attached to the first phenyl (methyl phenyl). The amide nitrogen is a different nitrogen (attached to the unsaturated acid). So the sulfonamide nitrogen is separate from the amide nitrogen. So step1 cleavage of sulfonamide yields the first phenyl amine and the aryl sulfonyl chloride (which still has the unsaturated amide attached). So step2 cleavage of amide yields the unsaturated acid (c2ccc(/C=C/COOH)cc2) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). The aryl sulfonyl chloride still has the unsaturated acid attached via the sulfonyl group? Actually the sulfonyl chloride is attached to the second phenyl (c2...). The unsaturated acid is attached to that phenyl via the side chain. So the sulfonyl chloride precursor after step1 is ClSO2-c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2. After step2, we break the amide, giving ClSO2-c2ccc(/C=C/COOH)cc2 (aryl sulfonyl chloride with unsaturated acid) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). Good.

Step3: Doebner modification retrosynthesis: break the α,β-unsaturated acid to give aromatic aldehyde (c2ccc(CHO)cc2) and malonic acid (HOOC-CH2-COOH). So precursor: aromatic aldehyde (c2ccc(CHO)cc2) and malonic acid.

Thus final three steps: 1) sulfonamide formation (forward) -> retrosynthesis: target -> 4-methyl aniline + aryl sulfonyl chloride (ClSO2-aryl). 2) amide formation (forward) -> retrosynthesis: aryl sulfonyl chloride with unsaturated amide -> aryl sulfonyl chloride with unsaturated acid + aniline. 3) Doebner modification (forward) -> retrosynthesis: aryl sulfonyl chloride with unsaturated acid -> aryl sulfonyl chloride aldehyde + malonic acid.

Now we need to produce JSON route with three reaction nodes. Need template IDs for each step. We have template ID 401931 corresponds to amide formation (looks like amide formation from acid and amine with double bond). That template seems to be amide formation with α,β-unsaturated acid? The template's retro_smarts: [#7:2]-[C;H0;D3;+0:1](=[O;D1;H0:3])/[CH;D2;+0:4]=[C:5]>>C-C(-C)(-C)-O-[C;H0;D3;+0:1](-[#7:2])=[O;D1;H0:3].O-C(=O)-[CH;D2;+0:4]=[C:5] . This seems to be amide formation from acid and amine where the acid is α,β-unsaturated (C=C). So we can use template 401931 for step2.

We need template for sulfonamide formation. Search.
